# New-ManualAcceptanceBundle.ps1

Generates the manual physical-acceptance bundles required by Requirements 26 and 29. It copies only an existing real MSI, self-contained publish outputs, and the real acceptance scripts; it never invents update/rollback packages. Every bundle contains the shared `AcceptanceContracts.ps1` dependency used by the result collector; Windows 10 bundles additionally contain `Verify-Windows10PhysicalAcceptance.ps1` and `Finalize-Windows10PhysicalAcceptance.ps1`. The read-only preflight emits a unique `windows10-preflight-<guid>.json` with create-new semantics under the user-approved EvidenceRoot; final composition requires that exact report, the complete elevated Release privileged capability matrix from a physical Windows 10 22H2 x64 host, and the eleven-case physical installer manifest. VM/Stage A evidence is not accepted. The finalizer can resolve the contract from the repository during development or from the bundle-local copy on a target machine. Without `-AllowIncompleteBundle`, missing base/updated/rollback MSI inputs or published outputs fail closed. Generated directories live under ignored `artifacts/manual/` and contain a non-eligible bundle manifest, payload SHA-256 manifest, README, target verification, human confirmation runner, result collector, and explicit cleanup script. The README uses the shared TestLab `.storage-chronicle-testlab-marker.json` contract for the dedicated data root.

The generator performs no installation, service registration, physical-machine mutation, VirtualBox installation, or deletion. It has no force/overwrite mode: an existing target bundle is preserved and generation fails with guidance to select a new `OutputRoot`. JSON manifests use the shared atomic create-only writer, and the README uses `FileMode.CreateNew` plus write-through.

Tests: PowerShell parser validation, strict missing-input failure, and preparation-bundle manifest/hash inspection.
